MacroTracker.description: Monitor when the 'market plumbing' is about to break. The Net Liquidity Index is the single most important number for 2026.

sofrSpread.threshold: Above 20 bps - banks desperate for cash

green.title: Green (Healthy)
green.description: Net Liquidity Index ≥ $3T. Market liquidity conditions are healthy. The financial system has sufficient reserves to handle normal operations and stress.

yellow.title: Yellow (Warning)
yellow.description: Net Liquidity Index between $2T and $3T. Market liquidity is becoming constrained. Monitor closely as conditions may deteriorate.

red.title: Red (Critical)
red.description: Net Liquidity Index < $2T. Market liquidity is critically low. The 'market plumbing' is at risk of breaking, which could lead to volatility, funding stress, or systemic issues.

netLiquidity.title: Net Liquidity Index
netLiquidity.description: The most important metric for 2026. Calculated as Fed Balance Sheet minus Treasury General Account minus Reverse Repo. This represents the actual liquidity available in the financial system. When this number drops too low, the market's ability to function smoothly is at risk.

rrp.title: Reverse Repo (RRP) Balance
rrp.description: Money market funds and other institutions parking excess cash with the Fed overnight. High RRP balances indicate excess liquidity in the system. When RRP drains, that liquidity moves into the broader market.

bankReserves.title: Bank Reserves
bankReserves.description: Cash that commercial banks hold at the Federal Reserve. These reserves are the foundation of the banking system's ability to lend and meet withdrawal demands. Declining reserves can signal tightening conditions.

fedBalanceSheet.title: Fed Balance Sheet
fedBalanceSheet.description: Total assets held by the Federal Reserve, primarily Treasury securities and mortgage-backed securities. The size of the balance sheet directly impacts system-wide liquidity. Quantitative tightening (QT) reduces this, tightening liquidity.

tga.title: Treasury General Account (TGA)
tga.description: The Treasury's checking account at the Fed. When the TGA increases, money is drained from the banking system. When it decreases (through spending), money flows back into the system, increasing liquidity.

treasury10Y.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield
treasury10Y.description: The interest rate on 10-year U.S. government bonds. This is a key indicator of borrowing costs and market expectations. Rising yields can indicate tightening financial conditions or inflation expectations.

sofrIorbSpread.title: SOFR-IORB Spread
sofrIorbSpread.description: The difference between the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) and the Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB). If SOFR spikes above IORB (spread > 20 bps), it means banks are desperate for cash and willing to pay more than the Fed's 'safe' rate to get it. This is a critical early warning signal that the 'market plumbing' is blocked.

highYieldSpreads.title: High-Yield Credit Spreads
highYieldSpreads.description: The gap between risky corporate debt and 'safe' government bonds. Widening spreads indicate that lenders are becoming afraid of defaults—a key sign that the 'bottom' of the K-shaped economy is failing. This often precedes broader market stress.

vix.title: VIX (Volatility Index)
vix.description: While the VIX tracks stock market volatility, it serves as a proxy for bond market volatility (MOVE Index). High VIX levels often precede equity crashes and indicate market stress. It measures the 'heartbeat' of market fear.

descriptions.NVDA: Leader in AI chips and the "Omniverse" simulation platform. Provides high-performance GPUs and Jetson chips for autonomous machines and edge AI applications.
descriptions.ARM: Designs energy-efficient processor architectures. Arm-based chips are standard for mobile and low-power computing in robotics, enabling longer battery life and better performance.
descriptions.AMBA: Specializes in AI vision processors. Their CV3-AD chip combines perception and path planning on a single chip, making it essential for autonomous navigation.
descriptions.OUST: Leading provider of digital LiDAR sensors. Their sensors provide 3D vision for warehouse robots, autonomous vehicles, and industrial automation.
descriptions.LAZR: Develops advanced LiDAR technology for autonomous vehicles and robotics. Their sensors enable precise 3D mapping and obstacle detection.
descriptions.TER: Makes robots (Universal Robots) and semiconductor testing equipment. Every AI chip must be tested by Teradyne equipment before leaving the factory.
descriptions.STM: Produces microcontrollers with integrated Neural Processing Units (NPUs). Powers millions of smaller, cost-effective robots with on-device AI capabilities.
descriptions.6324_T: Dominates the market for "strain wave gears"—high-precision reducers that enable robotic joints to move smoothly and accurately with minimal backlash.
descriptions.300433_SZ: Formerly an Apple supplier, now pivoting to humanoid robot assembly and core components. Aims to be the "Foxconn of Robotics" for 2026.
descriptions.ROK: Provides software and hardware solutions for factories that build robots. Essential "shovel" company for industrial automation and manufacturing.
descriptions.U: Leading platform for "Sim-to-Real" training. AI models learn to walk and manipulate objects in Unity's virtual world before being deployed to physical robots.
descriptions.MSFT: Through Azure Robotics and specialized AI models, provides cloud infrastructure and "common sense" reasoning that helps robots understand human instructions.
descriptions.INTC: Develops AI processors and the OpenVINO toolkit for edge AI deployment. Major player in AI acceleration hardware and software solutions.
descriptions.QCOM: Leading provider of edge AI chips for mobile and robotics applications. Their Snapdragon processors power many autonomous systems and IoT devices.
descriptions.AMD: Produces AI accelerators and processors competing with NVIDIA. Their EPYC and Instinct series are used in AI training and inference workloads.
descriptions.CGNX: Leading manufacturer of machine vision systems for industrial automation. Their vision sensors enable robots to see, inspect, and guide manufacturing processes.
descriptions.MBLY: Pioneer in computer vision for autonomous vehicles. Their EyeQ chips process camera data to enable self-driving capabilities in millions of vehicles.
descriptions.ABB: Global leader in industrial robots and automation systems. Provides complete robotic solutions for manufacturing, logistics, and process industries.
descriptions.6954_T: World's largest manufacturer of industrial robots and CNC systems. Fanuc robots are used in automotive, electronics, and precision manufacturing worldwide.
descriptions.6506_T: Major producer of servo motors, motion controllers, and industrial robots. Yaskawa's precision motion control systems are essential for robotic accuracy.
descriptions.PATH: Leading provider of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) software. Enables businesses to automate repetitive tasks using AI-driven software robots.
descriptions.CCJ: World's largest publicly traded uranium company. As nuclear power experiences a renaissance for AI data centers, Cameco is a key supplier of the fuel needed for 24/7 carbon-free baseload power.
descriptions.CEG: Leading nuclear power operator in the US. Constellation Energy operates the largest fleet of nuclear reactors, providing carbon-free baseload power essential for AI data centers that require 24/7 electricity.
descriptions.7011_T: Global leader in energy infrastructure and industrial machinery. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries manufactures nuclear reactors, power generation equipment, and electrical transformers critical for grid modernization.
descriptions.LLY: Pharmaceutical giant and leader in GLP-1 weight-loss drugs (Mounjaro, Zepbound). As the obesity epidemic drives demand, Eli Lilly's "Fortress Balance Sheet" makes it a prime player in the longevity sector.
descriptions.NVO: Danish pharmaceutical company and pioneer in GLP-1 therapies (Ozempic, Wegovy). Novo Nordisk dominates the weight-loss drug market, with strong cash position and growing demand for longevity treatments.
descriptions.TMO: Global leader in life sciences and laboratory equipment. Thermo Fisher provides the "shovels" for biotech—clinical trial services, lab equipment, and delivery systems (auto-injectors) needed for GLP-1 drugs.
descriptions.LMT: World's largest defense contractor. Lockheed Martin benefits from increased military budgets and reshoring of supply chains. Long-term government contracts provide stability regardless of consumer spending cycles.
descriptions.GLD: SPDR Gold Trust, the largest gold ETF. In a K-shaped economy with geopolitical friction, gold serves as a hedge against currency debasement and provides a floor for "paper wealth" when liquidity plumbing breaks.
descriptions.SMR: First company to receive U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission certification for small modular reactor (SMR) design. NuScale's scalable nuclear solutions are ideal for AI data centers requiring 24/7 carbon-free baseload power.
descriptions.LEU: Only U.S. company licensed to produce High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium (HALEU), essential fuel for advanced nuclear reactors. Centrus holds a strategic monopoly position in the nuclear fuel supply chain.
descriptions.GE: Global leader in grid infrastructure and power generation equipment. General Electric manufactures electrical transformers, high-voltage gear, and grid modernization solutions critical for upgrading aging power infrastructure.
descriptions.NRGV: Energy storage solutions provider specializing in grid-scale storage systems. Energy Vault's technology helps stabilize the electrical grid as renewable energy and AI data centers increase demand volatility.
descriptions.BDX: Leading manufacturer of auto-injector delivery systems for GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. Becton Dickinson's medical devices are essential "shovels" for the longevity sector, providing recurring revenue from device sales.
descriptions.IQV: World's largest clinical research organization (CRO). IQVIA provides clinical trial services, data analytics, and regulatory support—essential infrastructure for biotech companies developing GLP-1 and other therapies.
descriptions.CTLT: Global leader in drug delivery systems and pharmaceutical manufacturing services. Catalent provides auto-injectors, manufacturing capabilities, and packaging solutions needed for GLP-1 drug commercialization.
descriptions.AMGN: Biotechnology giant with GLP-1 pipeline and fortress balance sheet. Amgen's strong cash position and drug development capabilities make it a prime player in the longevity sector, with potential acquisition targets.
descriptions.RTX: Major defense contractor and aerospace leader. Raytheon Technologies provides missiles, radar systems, and advanced defense technology. Long-term government contracts provide stability regardless of economic cycles.
descriptions.NOC: Leading defense technology company specializing in space systems, cybersecurity, and advanced aerospace solutions. Northrop Grumman's government contracts offer predictable revenue in an uncertain economic environment.
descriptions.GD: Diversified defense contractor providing submarines, tanks, IT services, and aerospace systems. General Dynamics' long-term government contracts and defense focus make it a stable hedge against economic volatility.
descriptions.NEM: World's largest gold mining company. Newmont Corporation provides direct exposure to physical gold, complementing GLD ETF with ownership of actual gold reserves and mining operations.
descriptions.AAPL: Technology giant known for consumer electronics, software, and services. Leader in smartphones, tablets, and personal computers with a strong ecosystem.
descriptions.GOOGL: Parent company of Google, dominating search, advertising, cloud computing, and AI research. Major player in autonomous vehicles and quantum computing.
descriptions.AMZN: E-commerce and cloud computing behemoth. AWS is the leading cloud infrastructure provider, while Amazon dominates online retail and logistics.
descriptions.META: Social media and virtual reality company. Operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and is investing heavily in the metaverse and AI infrastructure.
descriptions.TSLA: Electric vehicle and clean energy company. Leading manufacturer of EVs and energy storage solutions, with ambitions in autonomous driving and robotics.
